_comment: Work-summary Stop hook: OPTIONAL. Merge this `hooks` block into your .claude/settings.json only
if you want this project's daily work summary brought up to date automatically when a session
stops. It is a separate file from settings.hooks.example.json on purpose: wiring the
constitutional gate must never switch this on as a side effect.
What it does: on each Stop event, .claude/hooks/work-summary-stop.py checks whether today's
commits or plan files are already reflected in workSummaries/daily/<today>.md. If not, it runs
`claude --print` as @work-summarizer in the background. Each run is an ordinary Claude Code run
against your account, so the hook skips whenever nothing has changed since its last run.
No conversation is left behind: the run uses --no-session-persistence, so Claude Code saves no
session and no session list shows it. The run's full output is kept instead under
<claude config dir>/logs/agentteams-work-summary/<project>-<hash>/runs/ for 14 days
(AGENTTEAMS_WS_KEEP_DAYS; 0 keeps none). The decision log is hook.log in the same folder.
The unattended run's tool set is capped (--tools) to Read, Grep, Glob, Agent, Edit and Write. No
other tool exists in it or in the agents it calls: no shell, no web tools, no cross-session
messaging, no scheduled or remote triggers, no worktree creation. The hook collects the git
evidence itself and hands it over as a file. No MCP server is loaded.
Within those six tools the run is in dontAsk permission mode and is granted reads, searches, the
Agent tool and writes under workSummaries/ only. That grant ADDS to the allow rules in your own
settings and cannot cap them, so: deny rules block credential files and edits under .claude/ and
.github/; and the hook refuses to launch, with a line in hook.log, if your user, project or local
settings allow Edit/Write outside workSummaries/ or a tool it does not know. Like every hook, the
run is outside the OS sandbox, and it reads commit messages and plan files others may have
written: look at the workSummaries/ diff before you push.
Claude Code saves no transcript for the run, but when the run calls an agent it still leaves a
small folder of agent metadata stubs under <claude config dir>/projects/. No session list shows
them.
The command below carries the SHA-256 of the script as emitted. On every Stop it re-hashes
.claude/hooks/work-summary-stop.py and runs it only on a match; otherwise it prints an error and
launches nothing. So an edit to the script (by an agent, or by a later --update --merge) stops
the hook until you review the script and merge this block again. settings.json, which holds the
digest, is the file Claude Code itself guards.
Check the first live run: if your summarizer needs more, set AGENTTEAMS_WS_ALLOWED_TOOLS rather
than editing the script, which --update --merge replaces. Project-specific instructions go in
extra.md in the run folder named above (your config directory, not the repository).
If a user-level Stop hook already launches a summarizer for this project, remove this project
from it BEFORE wiring this block, or both will launch. Any other harness that runs this
project's .claude/settings.json hooks will fire this hook too. A scheduler can call the script
directly: python3 .claude/hooks/work-summary-stop.py --foreground --project <project root>.
To switch it off without unwiring: AGENTTEAMS_WS_DISABLE=1. To remove it: delete the Stop entry.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import hashlib,runpy,sys;p,h=sys.argv[1:3];sys.argv=[p];hashlib.sha256(open(p,'rb').read()).hexdigest()==h or sys.exit('work-summary-stop.py does not match the digest recorded in settings.json: review the script, then merge settings.worksummary.example.json again');runpy.run_path(p,run_name='__main__')" "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/work-summary-stop.py" __LAUNCHER_SHA256__
